steps.what: Verify style costs, quantities and commercial assumptions for prices
Calculate style cost and margin scenarios
Determine prices after checking margin calculations and collection positioning

tasks.design: Configure a protected calculation sheet in {SPREADSHEET} before building custom pricing code. Checked inputs produce cost and margin scenarios; the designer checks calculations and positioning before recording the exact internal price version in {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated arithmetic can be mixed with judgement and changing cost assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed formulas can calculate scenarios once inputs and units are explicit.
tasks.still_hard: A target margin does not establish customer willingness to pay.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing collection coherence, perceived value and commercial risk.
tasks.altitude: Spends less time repeating arithmetic while retaining pricing judgement.

evidence.claim: Configured formulas can calculate style cost and margin scenarios over checked inputs; the local time estimate is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is designer pricing through internal recording; supplier quotation work, commercial release and sales negotiation retain their own time.

Designer in s1 captures style/version, component quantities and units, current unit costs, currency, tax treatment, wastage, channel fees and scenario margin definitions from cost records and policy. Missing fields require manual clarification within s1; no calculation runs on guessed values.
Cost owners maintain source records in their ordinary work; no new supplier or finance data service is assumed. Extra integration support is counted below.
Test native costing and protected spreadsheet formulas first; existing automated arithmetic earns no saving.
research_questions: After input verification and upkeep, how much repeated scenario arithmetic remains removable?

already_counted.description: Input capture and price calculation review and decision

incremental.description: Maintain formula tests and pricing assumptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact style/version, currency, channel, effective date, price and cost scenario snapshot; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+40=70, gross=30, focal upkeep=6, net=24. Range 0-8 assumes some repeated style scenarios; a native calculator already in use yields no arithmetic saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and market a product group

steps.what: Develop products or accessories and agree their marketing proposition and factual details
Lay out product sheets for boutiques or catalogs
Check product proofs and market the collection through chosen venues

tasks.design: Use a locked template in {DOCS} to produce sheets from content captured while developing the collection. The designer checks each proof before sharing it and keeps all venue negotiation and product development time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated product-sheet layout can consume time alongside creative and commercial work.
tasks.enabler_now: Template tools can populate variants from fixed fields.
tasks.still_hard: Creating a coherent collection and persuading venues to carry it.
tasks.human_edge: Product taste and relationships with retailers.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated sheet layout; product and channel decisions remain human.

evidence.claim: Figma Buzz locks template areas and populates variants from spreadsheet data.
Applying template-driven sheets to a fashion collection is an unmeasured local design.

assumptions: Boundary includes focal development and marketing participation, not retailer buying decisions, manufacturing or order fulfilment.

Designer in s1 captures product ID/version, approved description, image file and usage permission, materials, sizes and applicable price terms; capture and checking retain all s1 time. Missing facts are obtained manually in s1 or omitted from the sheet.
Native templates are tested before custom layout; no generated stock or availability claims are added.
Marketing conversation time is unchanged; retailer responses arise during s3, not as free advance structured input.
research_questions: Are variant sheets repeated enough to repay field capture and template maintenance?

already_counted.description: Content capture, proof review, development and venue engagement

approvals.approved_version: Exact sheet proof, product facts, images, terms and recipient set; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+0+15=80, gross=20, focal upkeep=6, net=14. Range 0-4 requires recurring template layouts; one-off bespoke artwork or existing automation yields little or no gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify custom clothing requirements, wearer needs and production constraints
Sketch alternative clothing and accessories concepts for the custom brief

loop.purpose: Draft visual concept alternatives within the custom brief
loop.input: Checked brief and permitted visual references
loop.output: Concept sketches with brief constraints and unresolved feasibility questions
loop.check: Designer compares silhouette, wearer context and every stated constraint, rejects impossible construction and misleading detail
loop.stop: One small concept batch and one correction; then sketch manually if unsuitable
loop.why_not_simpler: Visual concept generation is creative interpretation, not fixed template filling

steps.what: Refine custom concepts into a feasible design with client feedback

tasks.design: Retain the brief and client discussion in {DOCS}; optionally draft visual alternatives using an image-design tool in {OTHER}. The designer checks and redraws concepts for construction feasibility before presenting a custom proposal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exploratory sketch alternatives require creative effort before a client can compare them.
tasks.enabler_now: Image-generation tools can draft editable visual starting points, without proving fit or construction.
tasks.still_hard: Wearer movement, garment fit and buildable details need design expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Translating a person's or production's needs into a coherent, feasible garment.
tasks.altitude: More attention to feasibility and client interpretation; decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss costume movement and scene continuity

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images with Content Credentials.
Using image drafts for garment concepts does not establish wearable fit or labour savings; both need local testing.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the custom proposal; pattern construction, fittings, manufacture and client approval time remain separate and unchanged.

Designer in s1 captures purpose, wearer needs, movement, budget, deadline, dimensions when needed and permitted reference files; capture and permission checking are counted in s1. Missing requirements are clarified manually before drafting.
OTHER is an image-design tool; test native capabilities first. No wearer likeness or confidential production asset is supplied without suitable access arrangements.
Client feedback is obtained during s3; it is not assumed available at the first draft. Generated concepts are not manufacturing patterns.
unknowns: Client acceptance of generated concept drafts
research_questions: Does a concept trial save sketch time after feasibility corrections and client interpretation?

already_counted.description: Brief capture, visual checking and custom design refinement

incremental.description: Maintain reference permissions and draft constraints

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+40*0.70+25=88, gross=12, focal upkeep=6, net=6. Range 0-2 assumes a few useful visual drafts; extensive redraws remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather primary references and clarify clothing periods and production requirements
Compare clothing references and compile a cited styles research brief

loop.input: Source packet with identifiers, pages and production question
loop.output: Style comparisons with exact citations, uncertain dates and disagreements
loop.check: Designer opens every cited original, checks date, place, social context and distinction between depicted and everyday dress
loop.stop: One draft and correction; unsupported claims are removed or researched manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative and visual evidence needs contextual comparison rather than keyword matching alone

steps.what: Evaluate research against production needs and explain suitable period clothing choices

tasks.design: Search the existing {DOCS} archive first, then optionally compare a bounded source packet with a cited draft. The designer checks originals and distinguishes historical evidence from creative adaptation before recommending clothing choices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Historical evidence is dispersed and its relevance depends on place, period and social context.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded comparison can organise supplied sources with citations for review.
tasks.still_hard: Sources may depict exceptional dress or contain uncertain dating.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting visual and historical context in relation to the production's artistic needs.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated comparison writing; historical and artistic judgement remain human.

reach.task: Compare period context across costume and setting
reach.learn: Source criticism and continuity of visual context

evidence.claim: A source-bounded clothing research comparison is plausible; accuracy and time savings require local evaluation.

assumptions: Boundary covers designer research and recommendations, not archive staff work or subsequent costume construction.

Designer in s1 obtains permitted sources and captures source ID, page or image reference, provenance, stated date/place and production question. Unknown dates remain unknown; source gathering and extraction retain all s1 time.
Native archive search is tested first; no automatic access to uncatalogued collections is assumed.
Image interpretation failures return to manual comparison, with no invented historical source or citation.
unknowns: Quality and permission status of archive sources
research_questions: Does source checking plus correction leave a net reduction in period comparison work?

already_counted.description: Source collection, claim verification and production interpretation

incremental.description: Maintain citation checks and source packet conventions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+40*0.70+30=88, gross=12, focal upkeep=6, net=6. Range 0-2 assumes recurring accessible source comparisons; poor scans or extensive archive work eliminate the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retains artistic and commercial judgement while testing narrow arithmetic, layout and draft support.
reach: Connect product costs, garment feasibility and period research with adjacent design disciplines
role.ambitious_version: A designer who devotes more attention to feasible concepts and well-supported collection decisions.
